Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with the
causal curves and the relations $\le$, $\ll$, $I^{\pm}$, $J^{\pm}$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. All curves below are curves in
that sense.

**(a) Chronology and causality.** $(M,g,N)$ is **chronological** when there is
no $p\in M$ with $p\ll p$, equivalently when there is no nonconstant future
timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)$. It is **causal**
when there is no nonconstant future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with
$\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)$; a nonconstant future causal curve with equal endpoints
is called a **closed causal curve**, and a closed future timelike curve is
called a **closed timelike curve**.

**(b) Strong causality.** $(M,g,N)$ is **strongly causal** when for every
$p\in M$ and every open set $U\subseteq M$ with $p\in U$ there is an open set
$V$ with $p\in V\subseteq U$ such that for every future causal curve
$\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ and all $a\le s<t\le b$ with $\gamma(s)\in V$ and
$\gamma(t)\in V$ one has $\gamma([s,t])\subseteq V$. Thus no causal curve can
leave $V$ and later re-enter it; a set $V$ with this property for all causal
curves is called **causally convex for causal curves that meet it twice**.

**(c) Global hyperbolicity.** $(M,g,N)$ is **globally hyperbolic** when it is
strongly causal and for all $p,q\in M$ the **causal diamond**
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ is compact in the subspace topology
([[def-compact-space]]).

**(d) Time functions.** A **time function** on $(M,g,N)$ is a function
$u:M\to\mathbb R$ which is continuous ([[def-continuity-real]]) and satisfies
$u(\gamma(a))<u(\gamma(b))$ for every future causal curve
$\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $a<b$ that is not constant on $[a,b]$.

**(e) Temporal functions.** A **temporal function** on $(M,g,N)$ is a smooth
function $u:M\to\mathbb R$ ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]])
whose gradient is past-directed timelike: writing $du$ for its differential
([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]) and $\nabla u$ for the vector field
with $g(\nabla u,X)=du(X)$ for every smooth vector field $X$, constructed from
the inverse metric of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]], one
has
$$g(\nabla u,\nabla u)<0\qquad\text{and}\qquad du(N)=g(\nabla u,N)>0 .$$
The first inequality says that the gradient is nowhere zero and timelike; the
second fixes it as past-directed for the chosen time orientation. No level set
of a temporal function is asserted here to be a hypersurface or to be
spacelike, and no relation between temporal functions and compactness is
asserted; those claims are proved separately where they are used.

**(f) Scope and conventions.** These are mathematical conditions on the
Lorentzian model. Different sources define global hyperbolicity by equivalent
but differently phrased conditions; this page fixes the formulation of (c)
and proves the implications it uses. In particular no equivalence between
global hyperbolicity and the existence of a Cauchy hypersurface is asserted
by this definition, and the physical reading of strong causality or global
hyperbolicity as predictability of a classical model is adopted only in the
framework postulates.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with the
causal curves of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]], and let
$S\subseteq M$.

**(a) Spacelike hypersurfaces.** A subset $\Sigma\subseteq M$ is a **spacelike
embedded hypersurface** when it is an embedded three-dimensional submanifold
of $M$ ([[def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart]]) such that the
restriction of $g_p$ to $T_p\Sigma\times T_p\Sigma$ is positive definite for
every $p\in\Sigma$; equivalently, every nonzero vector tangent to $\Sigma$ is
spacelike ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). A spacelike
embedded hypersurface is automatically a nondegenerate hypersurface, so its
$g$-orthogonal complement in $T_pM$ is one-dimensional and nondegenerate, and
it carries a unique future-directed unit timelike normal; that normal is
constructed where it is used, not here.

**(b) Achronality and acausality.** $S$ is **achronal** when no two distinct
points $p,q\in S$ satisfy $p\ll q$ or $q\ll p$; $S$ is **acausal** when no two
distinct points $p,q\in S$ satisfy $p\le q$ or $q\le p$. Every acausal set is
achronal, since $p\ll q$ implies $p\le q$.

**(c) Cauchy sets.** $S$ is a **Cauchy set** when for every inextendible
causal curve $\gamma:I\to M$ the parameter set
$$\gamma^{-1}[S]:=\{t\in I:\gamma(t)\in S\}$$
has exactly one element. Because a strictly increasing continuous surjection
of intervals induces a bijection of parameter sets, this condition is
invariant under reparametrization
([[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (e)); it is stated in terms of
parameters rather than of the point set $\gamma(I)\cap S$, so that a closed
causal curve counts two visits to the same point as two parameter values. A
**Cauchy hypersurface** is a Cauchy set that is also a spacelike embedded
hypersurface in the sense of clause (a).

**(d) Domains of dependence.** For any $S\subseteq M$ define
$$D^+(S):=\{p\in M:\text{every past-inextendible causal curve through }p \text{ meets }S\},$$
and dually $D^-(S):=\{p\in M:\text{every future-inextendible causal curve
through }p\text{ meets }S\}$, where "meets $S$" means that some parameter
value is mapped into $S$, and $D(S):=D^+(S)\cup D^-(S)$ is the **domain of
dependence** of $S$.

**(e) Cauchy horizon.** For a closed set $S\subseteq M$ the **future Cauchy
horizon** is
$$H^+(S):=D^+(S)\setminus I^-(D^+(S)),$$
the set of points of $D^+(S)$ that are not chronologically preceded by any
point of $D^+(S)$; dually $H^-(S):=D^-(S)\setminus I^+(D^-(S))$, and the
**Cauchy horizon** is $H(S):=H^+(S)\cup H^-(S)$.

**(f) Scope.** These are mathematical definitions. Neither existence of
Cauchy sets nor any relation between the objects defined here is asserted.

derivations.claim: (The curve is a unit timelike geodesic.) Write $y(s):=(s,z_0)$ for the coordinate path of $\gamma$. Then $\dot y=(1,0,0,0)$ and $\ddot y=0$, so the geodesic equation holds by [L2] because the Christoffel symbols vanish; hence $\gamma$ is a geodesic with affine parameter $s$. Its tangent is $\gamma'(s)=\partial_0$, with $g(\gamma',\gamma')=\eta(\partial_0,\partial_0)=-1<0$ and $g(\gamma',N)=-1<0$; so it is future unit timelike and the chart geodesic equation is $\ddot y=0$. This is (i).

(Affine and length computations.) By step 1.1, $\sqrt{-g(\gamma',\gamma')}=1$ on $(0,1)$; the length of the segment over $[s_1,s_2]$ is therefore $\int_{s_1}^{s_2}1\,ds=s_2-s_1$, equal to the affine separation, and [L3] gives the metric-defined proper-time increment $(s_2-s_1)/c$. Under the SI interpretation stated in (ii), this has units seconds because $s_2-s_1$ is measured in metres and $c$ in $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$. If the curve is also an ideal-clock worldline, the separate postulate in (ii) identifies this duration with the difference in clock readings. This proves (ii).

(Maximal domain, limit point and conclusion.) By [L4] no geodesic of $M$ with the data of $\gamma$ extends the parameter interval beyond $(0,1)$, and $\gamma$ does not converge to a point of $M$ as $s\to1$: its coordinate $x^0(\gamma(s))=s$ tends to $1$, while every point of $M$ has $x^0\in(0,1)$. Hence $\gamma$, restricted to the maximal geodesic domain $(0,1)$, is future-inextendible in the sense of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (d) and its affine parameter is bounded above; the slab is timelike geodesically incomplete. By [L4] the slice $\Sigma_{1/2}$ is a Cauchy hypersurface and the model is globally hyperbolic, which is (iii) and (iv).

citations.quote:
**(a) The underlying manifold.** Let $M:=\mathbb R^4$ be Euclidean four-space
as a set and real vector space ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), equipped
with its standard smooth structure, in which the identity map
$x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3):M\to\mathbb R^4$ is a global smooth chart
([[def-smooth-manifold]],
[[prop-open-subsets-of-euclidean-space-have-the-standard-smooth-structure]]).
The coordinate vector fields $\partial_a:=\partial/\partial x^a$,
$a=0,1,2,3$, are smooth vector fields on $M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]), and at every
$p\in M$ the tuple
$(\partial_0|_p,\partial_1|_p,\partial_2|_p,\partial_3|_p)$ is a basis of
$T_pM$ ([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]).

**(b) The metric.** The **flat metric** $\eta$ is the smooth covariant
$2$-tensor field on $M$ whose components in the chart $x$ are the constant
functions $\eta_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]), that is
$$\eta=-(dx^0)^2+(dx^1)^2+(dx^2)^2+(dx^3)^2 .$$
It is symmetric, and at every $p$ its matrix in the basis of (a) is
$\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$: diagonal, with one negative and three positive
entries and no zero entry. Hence $\eta_p$ is nondegenerate with inertia
$(3,1,0)$, that is, a Lorentz form on $T_pM$
([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]), and $(M,\eta)$ is a smooth Lorentzian
four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). The restriction of $\eta_p$ to
$\operatorname{span}(\partial_1|_p,\partial_2|_p,\partial_3|_p)$ is positive
definite.

**(c) Time orientation.** The field $N:=\partial_0$ satisfies
$\eta(N,N)=-1<0$ pointwise, so $N$ is a time orientation of $(M,\eta)$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] clause (c)). The triple $(M,\eta,N)$ is
the **flat model**. At every $p$ the pointwise vocabulary of
[[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] and
[[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]] applies, and a nonzero causal
$v\in T_pM$ is future-directed exactly when $\eta_p(v,N_p)<0$
([[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]).

**(d) Events, displacements and straight paths.** The points of $M$ are the
**events** of the model. Since $M=\mathbb R^4$ is a vector space, for events
$p,q\in M$ the **displacement** from $p$ to $q$ is the vector $q-p\in M$, and
the **straight path** from $p$ to $q$ is the curve $s\mapsto p+s(q-p)$ on
$[0,1]$, whose chart representative has the constant velocity $q-p$. For
$v\in\mathbb R^4$ the **translation** is the map $\tau_v(p):=p+v$ of $M$.

**(e) Inertial charts and frames.** A chart of $M$ with domain $M$ is called a
**global chart**. A global chart $y=(y^0,y^1,y^2,y^3):M\to\mathbb R^4$ is
**inertial** when its components of $\eta$ are the constant functions
$\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ on $M$ and its first coordinate vector field
$\partial/\partial y^0$ is future-directed at every point. The chart $x$ of (a)
is inertial: its components of $\eta$ are $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ by
(b), and its first coordinate vector field is $N$, future-directed by (c). If
$y$ is inertial and $o\in M$, the tuple
$(o;\partial/\partial y^0|_o,\partial/\partial y^1|_o,
\partial/\partial y^2|_o,\partial/\partial y^3|_o)$ is an **inertial frame**
at $o$; its vectors satisfy
$\eta(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ and $e_0$ is
future-directed.

**(f) Cone sets.** Let a vector $v\in T_pM$ have coordinates
$(v^0,v^1,v^2,v^3)$ in an inertial chart, write $v_s:=(v^1,v^2,v^3)$ and
$|v_s|:=\sqrt{(v^1)^2+(v^2)^2+(v^3)^2}$
([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). Write
$$C^+:=\{v\in\mathbb R^4:v^0>|v_s|\}$$
and $\overline{C^+}:=\{v\in\mathbb R^4:v^0\ge|v_s|\}$ for the coordinate cone
sets. In every inertial chart and at every event $p$,
the future cone $C_p^+$ of (c) consists of exactly those $v$ with
$v^0>|v_s|$, its closure of exactly those with $v^0\ge|v_s|$, and the
future-directed causal vectors of $T_pM$ are exactly the nonzero vectors with
$v^0\ge|v_s|$; moreover the future cone is closed under sums. All of this is
proved in [[lem-gr-flat-inertial-cone-criterion-and-sums]], where the
independence of the inertial chart is also established.

**(g) Scope.** This is a mathematical definition; it asserts nothing about
nature. The physical reading of the flat model is recorded with the framework
postulates of this library and is not part of this definition, and the flat
examples and counterexamples of this page are conditional statements inside
the model.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let
$(U,x)$ be a smooth chart of $M$ in which every metric component
$g_{ab}=g(\partial_a,\partial_b)$ is a constant function on $U$. Then:

**(a)** Every Christoffel symbol of $\nabla$ in the chart vanishes
identically on $U$,
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=0$ ([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b)** The curvature tensor of $\nabla$ vanishes identically on $U$,
$R=0$ ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]],
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]]).

**(c)** Every coordinate curve of the chart is a geodesic of $\nabla$; that
is, for fixed constants $c^1,c^2,c^3$ the curve $s\mapsto
x^{-1}(s,c^1,c^2,c^3)$ is a geodesic in the affine parameter $s$
([[prop-coordinate-geodesic-equation]]).

In coordinates $x^1,\ldots,x^n$, a smooth curve $\gamma$ is a geodesic if and only if, throughout every parameter subinterval lying in the chart,
$$\ddot x^k+\Gamma^k{}_{ij}(x)\dot x^i\dot x^j=0\qquad(1\le k\le n),$$
with summation over repeated indices.

Let $(V,\eta)$ be a Lorentz vector space of signature $(-,+,+,+)$
([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]), with associated quadratic form
$q(v)=\eta(v,v)$. A vector $v\in V$ is

- **timelike** when $q(v)<0$;
- **null**, or **lightlike**, when $v\neq 0$ and $q(v)=0$;
- **spacelike** when $q(v)>0$;
- **causal** when it is timelike or null.

The zero vector $0\in V$ satisfies $q(0)=0$ and is consequently **none** of
timelike, null or spacelike: the null case explicitly excludes it, and the
timelike and spacelike cases exclude it by $q(0)=0$ together with the strict
inequalities. The **causal character** of a nonzero vector $v$ is the sign of
the real number $q(v)$, and the three names are attached to the three signs as
above. When no confusion arises, the pairing $\eta$ itself is written
$\langle v,w\rangle:=\eta(v,w)$.

**Each nonzero vector has exactly one causal character.** For a nonzero
$v\in V$ the real number $q(v)$ satisfies exactly one of $q(v)<0$, $q(v)=0$,
$q(v)>0$ by trichotomy of the order on $\mathbb R$, so $v$ is timelike, null or
spacelike, and no two of the three alternatives can hold at once. The causal
vectors are therefore exactly the nonzero vectors that are timelike or null,
and the zero vector is causal in no sense introduced here.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). Write
$N_p^{\perp}=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,N_p)=0\}$
([[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]) and let $T_p$ be the
timelike set, with components $C_p^+$ (the one containing $N_p$) and $C_p^-$,
and with future and past causality as fixed in
[[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]] and
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]. Then:

1. $N_p^{\perp}$ is a $3$-dimensional linear subspace of $T_pM$, and $g_p$ is
   positive definite on it; equivalently, every nonzero $v\in T_pM$ with
   $g_p(v,N_p)=0$ is spacelike.
2. $g_p(v,N_p)\neq0$ for every nonzero causal $v\in T_pM$.
3. $C_p^+=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,v)<0\text{ and }g_p(v,N_p)<0\}$, and
   $C_p^-=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,v)<0\text{ and }g_p(v,N_p)>0\}$.
4. A nonzero $v\in T_pM$ is causal and future-directed if and only if
   $v\in\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)$, and causal and past-directed if and only if
   $v\in\operatorname{cl}(C_p^-)$. Consequently
   $\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)\setminus\{0\}$ is exactly the set of
   future-directed causal vectors and $\operatorname{cl}(C_p^-)\setminus\{0\}$
   exactly the set of past-directed causal vectors,
   $\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)\cap\operatorname{cl}(C_p^-)=\{0\}$, and every
   nonzero causal vector is exactly one of future-directed and past-directed.

Let $(V,\eta)$ be a Lorentz vector space of signature $(-,+,+,+)$
([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]), with causal terminology as in
[[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], and let

$$T:=\{v\in V:\eta(v,v)<0\}$$

be its **timelike set**. Components and closures refer to the topology obtained
by using any ordered basis to identify $V$ with Euclidean $\mathbb R^4$;
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]], step 5.1, proves that the
resulting open sets are independent of the basis. By that lemma the
set $T$ has exactly two connected components, and each of them is nonempty,
open, convex and path-connected. A **time orientation** of $(V,\eta)$ is a
choice of one of these two components. Fixing such a choice, write $C^+$ for the
chosen component and

$$C^-:=T\setminus C^+$$

for the other component; thus $T=C^+\sqcup C^-$ is a disjoint union and
$C^+$, $C^-$ are exactly the two components supplied by the lemma. Relative to
this choice a vector $v\in V$ is

- **future timelike** when $v\in C^+$;
- **past timelike** when $v\in C^-$;
- **future null** when $v\neq 0$, $\eta(v,v)=0$ and $v\in\operatorname{cl}(C^+)$;
- **past null** when $v\neq 0$, $\eta(v,v)=0$ and $v\in\operatorname{cl}(C^-)$;
- **future causal** when it is future timelike or future null;
- **past causal** when it is past timelike or past null.

The sets $\operatorname{cl}(C^+)$ and $\operatorname{cl}(C^-)$ are the
**future closed cone** and the **past closed cone** of the time-oriented space
$(V,\eta,C^+)$. By [[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]] each of them
is a convex cone, their intersection is $\{0\}$, and a vector is causal exactly
when it is future causal or past causal, in which case exactly one of these two
alternatives holds: no nonzero vector is both future causal and past causal.
The timelike vectors are exactly the points of $T=C^+\cup C^-$, and
$0\notin T$ because $\eta(0,0)=0$; since a null vector is nonzero with
$\eta(v,v)=0$, no vector is both timelike and null, so the classes above are
mutually exclusive where the definitions say they are: no vector is both future
and past causal, and no timelike vector is null.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary, so that $M$ is Hausdorff
and second countable and carries a maximal smooth atlas
([[def-smooth-manifold]]). Let $g$ be a smooth covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$
in the sense of [[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]. Then $g$ assigns
to every $p\in M$ a bilinear form $g_p:T_pM\times T_pM\to\mathbb R$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]).

**(a) Lorentzian metric.** The field $g$ is a **Lorentzian metric of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$** on $M$ when it is symmetric and nondegenerate, and at every
$p\in M$ the pair $(T_pM,g_p)$ is a Lorentz vector space of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ in the sense of [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]: that is, $g_p$ has
inertia $(3,1,0)$, so that some — equivalently every — basis of $T_pM$ in which
the matrix of $g_p$ is diagonal has exactly one negative and three positive
diagonal entries. The pair $(M,g)$ is a **smooth Lorentzian four-manifold** (or
Lorentzian manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$). In a smooth chart $(U,x)$ the
**components** of $g$ are the $C^\infty$ functions
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ of
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]], and $g_{ab}=g_{ba}$ by symmetry.
We use indices $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$ and the Einstein summation convention, with
components in a chart written as lower-case indexed symbols and equations
between indexed fields understood basis-independently. These conventions are
fixed once for this library and the physical reading of the symbols is recorded
with the framework postulates, separately from this mathematical definition.

**(b) Pointwise causal structure.** For every $p\in M$ the vocabulary of
[[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] applies to the Lorentz vector
space $(T_pM,g_p)$: a tangent vector $v\in T_pM$ is **timelike** when
$g_p(v,v)<0$, **null** when $v\neq0$ and $g_p(v,v)=0$, **spacelike** when
$g_p(v,v)>0$, and **causal** when it is timelike or null. Every nonzero
$v\in T_pM$ has exactly one causal character. The **timelike set**
$T_p:=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,v)<0\}$ has exactly two connected components, each
nonempty, open, convex and path-connected; each $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3$ of $T_pM$ satisfies $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$
for some ordering, so in particular nonzero orthonormal vectors exist at every
point ([[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]],
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]]).

**(c) Time orientation.** A **time orientation** of $(M,g)$, also called a
**choice of future cone**, is a smooth vector field $N$ on $M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]], whose tangent-bundle
smooth structure uses the axiom $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of
[[def-countable-choice]]; this is the only use of that axiom in this
definition) such that

$$g_p(N_p,N_p)<0\qquad\text{for every }p\in M .$$

The function $p\mapsto g_p(N_p,N_p)$ is $C^\infty$ because $g$ is a smooth
covariant $2$-tensor field and $N$ a smooth field, so the condition is a
pointwise strict inequality between a smooth function and $0$; since
$g_p(N_p,N_p)<0$ implies $N_p\neq0$, a time orientation is nowhere vanishing.
A **time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold** is a triple $(M,g,N)$
consisting of a smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and a time orientation $N$.

Given a time orientation $N$ and $p\in M$, the vector $N_p$ is timelike, and we
**define** a nonzero causal vector $v\in T_pM$ to be **future-directed** when
$g_p(v,N_p)<0$ and **past-directed** when $g_p(v,N_p)>0$. The classification of
nonzero causal vectors into exactly these two classes, and its agreement with
the two components of the timelike set (the future component is the component
$C_p^+$ containing $N_p$, and the future closed null cone is
$\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)\setminus\{0\}$), is proved in
[[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]; in particular no
nonzero causal $v$ satisfies $g_p(v,N_p)=0$, so the definition is exhaustive and
mutually exclusive. Replacing $N$ by $-N$ reverses every future/past label, and
two time orientations $N,N'$ determine the same future-directed causal vectors
at every point where $g_p(N_p,N'_p)<0$, while they determine opposite ones
where $g_p(N_p,N'_p)>0$, by
[[lem-gr-timelike-fields-define-equal-or-opposite-future-cones]]; that lemma
also shows the sign of $p\mapsto g_p(N_p,N'_p)$ is constant on every connected
component of $M$.

**(d) The inverse metric.** Because $g_p$ is nondegenerate, it induces at each
$p$ an isomorphism $\flat_p:T_pM\to T_p^*M$, $v\mapsto g_p(v,\cdot)$, and an
inverse metric $g_p^{-1}$ on the dual space; the inverse metric, the musical
isomorphisms and the components $g^{ab}$ are defined separately on this page,
where the smoothness of those components is also proved. Neither construction
uses any choice principle beyond the one already recorded in (c).


**(e) Smooth timelike curves and their scalar normalization.** Before using
these quantities in the physical conventions, fix a positive real scaling
parameter $c$ (with no physical meaning or dimension in this mathematical
item). A **smooth future timelike curve** is a smooth map $\gamma:I\to M$
from a nonempty open real interval $I$ ([[def-interval]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]) whose velocity derivation
$\gamma'(s)\in T_{\gamma(s)}M$
([[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]]) satisfies
$g(\gamma',\gamma')<0$ and $g(\gamma',N)<0$ at every $s\in I$.
In a chart its components are $d(x^a\circ\gamma)/ds$, $a=0,1,2,3$.
For a supplied base point $s_0\in I$ and additive constant $\tau_0\in\mathbb R$
define

$$h(s):=\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(s)}(\gamma'(s),\gamma'(s))},\qquad \tau(s):=\tau_0+\frac1c\int_{s_0}^{s}h(r)\,dr,\qquad U(s):=\frac{c\gamma'(s)}{h(s)}.$$

The integral is oriented when $s<s_0$. The function $\tau$ is called
**proper time** for this scaling and $U$ the **four-velocity** of the smooth
curve; its increment times $c$ is the Lorentzian length. The well-definedness
proof below shows $\tau'>0$, that $\tau:I\to\tau(I)$ is a smooth
diffeomorphism, and that $U$ is the velocity of $\gamma\circ\tau^{-1}$.
Thus $g(U,U)=-c^2$ and $U$ is future timelike. This introduces the smooth
case before any physical unit reading; the later worldline definition extends
it to its stated $C^k$, endpoint and piecewise-$C^1$ classes. It asserts no
clock coupling, motion law or physical value of $c$.

**Convention and scope.** The physical reading of a smooth time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold as a classical spacetime model, and the domain in which
that reading is adopted, are recorded in the framework postulate
`post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain`; the words spacetime and event carry no
mathematical content beyond this definition, and this item asserts no claim
about nature. The dimension $4$ and the absence of boundary are part of the
data; nothing in the definition assumes that $M$ is nonempty or connected, and
no completeness, extendibility or maximality property of $(M,g)$ is asserted.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty
open subset, carrying the restricted smooth structure of
[[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]].

**(a) Congruences.** An **observer congruence** on $U$ is a smooth vector field
$n$ on $U$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]) such that
$n_q$ is an observer at $q$ for every $q\in U$
([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]); explicitly,

$$g_q(n_q,n_q)=-1\quad\text{and}\quad g_q(n_q,N_q)<0\qquad\text{for every }q\in U .$$

Since $g_q(n_q,n_q)=-1$, the field $n$ is nowhere vanishing. A single observer
at a point is therefore not a congruence, and a congruence is not an ordered
basis or frame of $T_qM$.

**(b) Observer curves.** Because $n$ is a smooth vector field on $U$, the
theorem on maximal integral curves
([[thm-unique-maximal-integral-curve-through-each-point]],
[[def-integral-curve-of-a-vector-field]]) assigns to every $q\in U$ a unique
maximal integral curve $\gamma_q:I_q\to U$ of $n$ with $\gamma_q(0)=q$,
defined on an open interval $I_q\subseteq\mathbb R$. We call these curves the
**observers** (or **observer curves**) of the congruence. Each observer is
regular: $\gamma_q'(s)=n_{\gamma_q(s)}$ and $\lVert n\rVert_g=1$ at every
parameter value, so the tangent vector is unit timelike and future-directed at
every parameter value. Completeness of the maximal intervals $I_q$, and global
product or foliation structure of $U$, are not asserted. The parameter $s$ is
the flow parameter of $n$; it is not identified with any clock reading here.

**(c) Adapted charts.** An **$n$-adapted chart** is a smooth chart
$(u^0,u^1,u^2,u^3):U'\to\mathbb R^4$ of $M$ whose domain $U'$ is a nonempty
open subset of $U$ and whose **spatial coordinates** $u^1,u^2,u^3$ are constant
along every integral curve of $n$ contained in $U'$; equivalently, for every
$q\in U'$ the observer curve $\gamma_q$ satisfies
$u^i(\gamma_q(s))=u^i(q)$ for all $s$ with $\gamma_q(s)\in U'$ and
$i=1,2,3$. No global adapted chart, and no adapted chart on all of $U$, is
asserted by this definition; one exists near every point of $U$ by the
existence corollary proved on this page.

**(d) Scope.** A congruence is a field of observer directions on an open set; it
is not a chart, not a tetrad field, and not a family of parametrized
worldlines with specified domains. The physical reading of its observer curves
as ideal-clock worldlines, and the identification of the flow parameter with a
measurable time, belong to the physical postulates of the framework and are not
asserted here.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]).

**(a) Observers.** An **observer at $p$** is a tangent vector
$n\in T_pM$ such that $g_p(n,n)=-1$ and $n$ is future-directed in the sense of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], that is, $g_p(n,N_p)<0$. Because
$g_p(n,n)=-1\neq0$, an observer is timelike and in particular nonzero
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). Observers at $p$ exist:
the vector $N_p$ is timelike, and
$n:=N_p/\sqrt{-g_p(N_p,N_p)}$ satisfies $g_p(n,n)=-1$ and
$g_p(n,N_p)=-\sqrt{-g_p(N_p,N_p)}<0$, where the square root is the
nonnegative root of [[def-rational-power]]; then $-n$ is a unit timelike
vector with $g_p(-n,N_p)>0$, so it is not an observer, and the two vectors
$n,-n$ point in opposite time directions.

**(b) Rest space.** For an observer $n$ at $p$, the **rest space** of $n$ is
the $g_p$-orthogonal complement of the line $\mathbb Rn$,

$$n^{\perp}=\{v\in T_pM: g_p(v,n)=0\},$$

in the sense of [[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]. It is
a linear subspace of $T_pM$. The further facts that $\dim n^{\perp}=3$ and
that the restriction of $g_p$ to $n^{\perp}$ is positive definite are proved
in [[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]]; they are consequences, not
part of the definition.

**(c) Spatial projection.** The **spatial projection** of the observer $n$ is
the map

$$h_n:T_pM\longrightarrow T_pM,\qquad h_n(v):=v+g_p(n,v)\,n .$$

The map is linear because $g_p$ is bilinear, its image is contained in
$n^{\perp}$, and it fixes $n^{\perp}$ pointwise; that it is the
$g_p$-orthogonal projection onto $n^{\perp}$ with kernel $\mathbb Rn$ is
proved in [[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]].

**(d) Scope.** An observer at $p$ is a single tangent vector. It is not an
ordered basis or frame of $T_pM$, not a chart, not a field of observers such as
the congruences defined later on this page, and not a curve or a worldline: no
parametrized curve, clock reading, proper time or measurement is attached to
$n$ by this definition. The physical reading of an observer as the direction
of an ideal clock's worldline, and the measurement interpretation of the
observer-relative quantities introduced later on this page, belong to the
physical postulates and unit conventions of the framework and are not asserted
here.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let
$U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open subset.

**(a) Geodesic congruence.** A **smooth future unit timelike geodesic
congruence** on $U$ is an observer congruence $n$ on $U$
([[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]],
[[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]), so that
$g(n,n)=-1$ and $g(n,N)<0$ on $U$, which in addition is geodesic:
$$\nabla_nn=0\qquad\text{on }U .$$
Thus each observer curve of the congruence is an affinely parametrized
geodesic ([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]]) and its flow parameter is
affine; by [[lem-gr-parallel-transport-and-geodesic-speed]] the tangent is
future unit timelike at every parameter value.

**(b) Observer curves.** By [[thm-unique-maximal-integral-curve-through-each-point]]
each $q\in U$ lies on a unique maximal integral curve
$\gamma_q:I_q\to U$ of $n$ with $\gamma_q(0)=q$; these are the **observer
curves** or **flow lines** of the congruence, and their parameter $s$ is the
**affine parameter** of the geodesic. The mathematical proper-time function
$\tau$ of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]], normalized by
$\tau(0)=0$, satisfies
$$\tau(s_2)-\tau(s_1)=\frac{1}{c}\int_{s_1}^{s_2}\sqrt{-g(n,n)}\,ds=\frac{s_2-s_1}{c}\qquad(s_1<s_2,\ s_1,s_2\in I_q).$$
Thus $\tau(s)=s/c$ with this normalization. This is the metric-defined
mathematical proper-time parameter, not a clock reading; the ideal-clock
interpretation is a separate physical assumption.

**(c) Kinematic quantities.** On $U$ define the smooth covariant $2$-tensor
field
$$B_{ab}:=\nabla_bn_a,\qquad n_a:=g_{ab}n^b ,$$
the **rest-space metric field**
$$h_{ab}:=g_{ab}+n_an_b,$$
with index-raised field $h^{ab}:=g^{ab}+n^an^b$ built from the inverse metric
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]), and:
$$\theta:=g^{ab}B_{ab},\qquad \sigma_{ab}:=B_{(ab)}-\tfrac13\theta\,h_{ab},\qquad \omega_{ab}:=B_{[ab]},$$
the **expansion**, **shear** and **vorticity** of the congruence, where
$B_{(ab)}=\tfrac12(B_{ab}+B_{ba})$ and $B_{[ab]}=\tfrac12(B_{ab}-B_{ba})$.
The three fields $\theta$, $\sigma$, $\omega$ and the tensor $B$ are smooth
in every chart ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]), because
components of $\nabla n$, $g$ and $g^{-1}$ are smooth.

**(d) Scope.** The definition asserts no dynamical equation, no sign of
$\theta$ and no physical interpretation. In particular the identities making
$\sigma$ and $\omega$ rest-space tensors, their tracelessness and
antisymmetry, and the decomposition $B=\tfrac13\theta h+\sigma+\omega$ are
proved in [[lem-gr-kinematic-decomposition-identities]], not assumed here.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let
$U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open subset.

**(a) Geodesic congruence.** A **smooth future unit timelike geodesic
congruence** on $U$ is an observer congruence $n$ on $U$
([[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]],
[[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]), so that
$g(n,n)=-1$ and $g(n,N)<0$ on $U$, which in addition is geodesic:
$$\nabla_nn=0\qquad\text{on }U .$$
Thus each observer curve of the congruence is an affinely parametrized
geodesic ([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]]) and its flow parameter is
affine; by [[lem-gr-parallel-transport-and-geodesic-speed]] the tangent is
future unit timelike at every parameter value.

**(b) Observer curves.** By [[thm-unique-maximal-integral-curve-through-each-point]]

$\gamma_q:I_q\to U$ of $n$ with $\gamma_q(0)=q$; these are the **observer
curves** or **flow lines** of the congruence, and their parameter $s$ is the
**affine parameter** of the geodesic. The mathematical proper-time function
$\tau$ of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]], normalized by
$\tau(0)=0$, satisfies
$$\tau(s_2)-\tau(s_1)=\frac{1}{c}\int_{s_1}^{s_2}\sqrt{-g(n,n)}\,ds=\frac{s_2-s_1}{c}\qquad(s_1<s_2,\ s_1,s_2\in I_q).$$
Thus $\tau(s)=s/c$ with this normalization. This is the metric-defined
mathematical proper-time parameter, not a clock reading; the ideal-clock
interpretation is a separate physical assumption.

**(c) Kinematic quantities.** On $U$ define the smooth covariant $2$-tensor
field
$$B_{ab}:=\nabla_bn_a,\qquad n_a:=g_{ab}n^b ,$$
the **rest-space metric field**
$$h_{ab}:=g_{ab}+n_an_b,$$
with index-raised field $h^{ab}:=g^{ab}+n^an^b$ built from the inverse metric
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]), and:
$$\theta:=g^{ab}B_{ab},\qquad \sigma_{ab}:=B_{(ab)}-\tfrac13\theta\,h_{ab},\qquad \omega_{ab}:=B_{[ab]},$$
the **expansion**, **shear** and **vorticity** of the congruence, where
$B_{(ab)}=\tfrac12(B_{ab}+B_{ba})$ and $B_{[ab]}=\tfrac12(B_{ab}-B_{ba})$.
The three fields $\theta$, $\sigma$, $\omega$ and the tensor $B$ are smooth
in every chart ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]), because
components of $\nabla n$, $g$ and $g^{-1}$ are smooth.

**(d) Scope.** The definition asserts no dynamical equation, no sign of
$\theta$ and no physical interpretation. In particular the identities making
$\sigma$ and $\omega$ rest-space tensors, their tracelessness and
antisymmetry, and the decomposition $B=\tfrac13\theta h+\sigma+\omega$ are
proved in [[lem-gr-kinematic-decomposition-identities]], not assumed here.

Let $n$ be a geodesic congruence with kinematic quantities $B$, $\theta$,
$\sigma$, $\omega$ and $h$ on $U$ as in
[[def-gr-geodesic-congruence-and-kinematics]], and write
$h^{ab}:=g^{ab}+n^an^b$. Then, everywhere on $U$:

**(a)** $n^aB_{ab}=0$ and $B_{ab}n^b=0$; hence $B$ takes values in the
rest-space bundle $n^{\perp}$ in both slots
([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]).

**(b)** $h_{ab}n^b=0$, the restriction of $h$ to $n^{\perp}$ is positive
definite, $h^{ab}h_{bc}=\delta^a_c+n^an_c$, and $h_{ab}h^{ba}=3$.

**(c)** $\sigma_{ab}$ is symmetric and $h^{ab}\sigma_{ab}=0$;
$\omega_{ab}$ is antisymmetric; and
$B_{ab}=\tfrac13\theta\,h_{ab}+\sigma_{ab}+\omega_{ab}$.

**(d)** $B_{ab}B^{ba}=\tfrac13\theta^2+\sigma_{ab}\sigma^{ab}-\omega_{ab}\omega^{ab}$,
where all indices are raised with $g$; moreover
$\sigma_{ab}\sigma^{ab}\ge0$ and $\omega_{ab}\omega^{ab}\ge0$, the first
vanishing exactly when $\sigma=0$ and the second exactly when $\omega=0$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$U\subseteq M$ be open and let $n$ be a smooth future unit timelike geodesic
congruence on $U$ with kinematic quantities $B$, $\theta$, $\sigma$, $\omega$
and rest-space metric $h$
([[def-gr-geodesic-congruence-and-kinematics]]). Let $q\in U$ and let
$\gamma_q:I_q\to U$ be the observer curve through $q$ with affine parameter
$s$, $s\in I_q$ ([[thm-unique-maximal-integral-curve-through-each-point]]).

**(a) Raychaudhuri equation.** For every $s\in I_q$,
$$\frac{d}{ds}\theta(\gamma_q(s)) =-\tfrac13\theta(\gamma_q(s))^2-\sigma_{ab}\sigma^{ab}(\gamma_q(s)) +\omega_{ab}\omega^{ab}(\gamma_q(s))-\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}(\gamma_q(s))\,n^a(\gamma_q(s))\,n^b(\gamma_q(s)),$$
where all contractions use $g$ and $\operatorname{Ric}$ is the Ricci tensor
of the metric-selected connection
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]).

**(b) Focusing.** Suppose $\omega=0$ and
$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}n^an^b\ge0$ on $U$, and suppose there is
$s_0\in I_q$ with $\theta_0:=\theta(\gamma_q(s_0))<0$. Then
$\theta(\gamma_q(s))<0$ for every $s\in I_q$ with $s>s_0$, and
$$\frac{1}{-\theta(\gamma_q(s))}\le\frac{1}{-\theta_0}-\frac{s-s_0}{3}.$$
Consequently $s<s_0+3/(-\theta_0)$ for every such $s$, so
$\sup I_q\le s_0+3/(-\theta_0)$ for the maximal integral curve in $U$.
Any continuation beyond this bound that remains a smooth geodesic congruence
and continues to satisfy $\omega=0$ and $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}n^an^b\ge0$
along the continued flow line is impossible. A continuation outside $U$ that
does not preserve these hypotheses is not ruled out by this result.

derivations.claim: (The field is a smooth unit future timelike geodesic congruence.) On $O$ the function $\rho$ is smooth and strictly positive, and the components $W^a=(e^a-q^a)/\rho$ are smooth; by [L2], $\eta(W,W)=-1$ and $W$ is future-directed relative to the time-orientation field $N=\partial_0$. It remains to verify the geodesic condition. Put $y:=e-q$, so $y^0=T-t$ and $y^i=-z^i$. From $\rho^2=(T-t)^2-|z|_{\mathrm e}^2$ one computes $\partial_0\rho=-(T-t)/\rho=y_0/\rho$ and $\partial_i\rho=-z^i/\rho=y_i/\rho$, hence $\partial_b\rho=y_b/\rho$ with $y_b=\eta_{bc}y^c$; also $\partial_b y^a=-\delta^a_b$. Therefore $$\partial_bW^a=\partial_b\Bigl(\frac{y^a}{\rho}\Bigr)=-\frac{\delta^a_b}{\rho}-\frac{y^ay_b}{\rho^3}=-\frac{\delta^a_b}{\rho}-\frac{W^aW_b}{\rho}.$$ Using $y^by_b=\eta(y,y)=-\rho^2$, $$W^b\partial_bW^a=\frac{y^b}{\rho}\Bigl(-\frac{\delta^a_b}{\rho}-\frac{y^ay_b}{\rho^3}\Bigr)=-\frac{y^a}{\rho^2}-\frac{y^a(y^by_b)}{\rho^4}=-\frac{y^a}{\rho^2}+\frac{y^a}{\rho^2}=0.$$ Since the metric-selected connection of the flat model has vanishing Christoffel symbols in this chart, $\nabla_WW=0$; with [L3] the field $W$ is a smooth future unit timelike geodesic congruence. This proves (i).

(The flow lines.) For fixed $p\in O$ define $\gamma(s):=e-(1-s/\rho(p))(e-p)$ for $s\in[0,\rho(p))$. Then $\gamma(0)=p$, $\gamma$ is affine in $s$ with derivative $\gamma'(s)=(e-p)/\rho(p)=W(p)$, a constant vector; by [L1] straight coordinate lines are geodesics, so $s\mapsto\gamma(s)$ is a geodesic of the model with $\gamma'(s)=W(p)$. Its $\rho$-value is $\rho(\gamma(s))=\sqrt{-\eta(e-\gamma(s),e-\gamma(s))}$; since $e-\gamma(s)=(1-s/\rho(p))(e-p)$, one gets $\rho(\gamma(s))=(1-s/\rho(p))\rho(p)=\rho(p)-s$, which is positive for $s<\rho(p)$ and vanishes at $s=\rho(p)$; in particular $\gamma(s)\in O$ for $0\le s<\rho(p)$ and $\gamma(\rho(p))=e$ in the ambient affine space $A$. Also $W(\gamma(s))=(e-\gamma(s))/\rho(\gamma(s))=(e-p)/\rho(p)=\gamma\prime(s)$, so it is an integral curve. Therefore $\gamma$ is the maximal forward flow line of $W$ through $p$, with $e$ as its limiting focal event at finite affine parameter $\rho(p)$. The same straight line continues for all real $s$ and is a geodesic of $A$ defined on all of $\mathbb R$ by [L1]. This proves (ii).

(The kinematic quantities.) By [L1] the connection is flat and $B_{ab}=\nabla_bW_a=\partial_bW_a$; from the computation in step 1.1, with $W_a=y_a/\rho$, $$B_{ab}=\partial_b\Bigl(\frac{y_a}{\rho}\Bigr)=-\frac{\eta_{ab}}{\rho}-\frac{y_ay_b}{\rho^3}=-\frac{1}{\rho}\bigl(\eta_{ab}+W_aW_b\bigr)=-\frac{h_{ab}}{\rho}.$$ In particular $B$ is symmetric, so $\omega_{ab}=B_{[ab]}=0$, and $B_{ab}W^b=-h_{ab}W^b/\rho=0$. For the expansion, [L4] and $g^{ab}h_{ab}=3$ give $\theta=g^{ab}B_{ab}=-\frac{1}{\rho}g^{ab}h_{ab}=-\frac{3}{\rho}$; then the shear is $\sigma_{ab}=B_{(ab)}-\tfrac13\theta h_{ab}=-\frac{h_{ab}}{\rho}+\frac{1}{\rho}h_{ab}=0$. This proves (iii).

(The focusing bound is attained and the congruence does not extend.) Let $\gamma=\gamma_p$ be the flow line of step 2.1 and write $\theta(s):=\theta(\gamma(s))$. By step 2.2 and $\rho(\gamma(s))=\rho(p)-s$, $\theta(s)=-3/(\rho(p)-s)$ for $0\le s<\rho(p)$. Hence $\theta_0:=\theta(p)=-3/\rho(p)<0$ and $$\frac{1}{-\theta(s)}=\frac{\rho(p)-s}{3}=\frac{1}{-\theta_0}-\frac{s}{3},$$ so the focusing bound of [L5] holds with equality for $s_0=0$. To see directly that this congruence field cannot extend continuously across its focal event $e$, use the translation identification of tangent spaces of $A=\mathbb R^4$ and set $v_1:=\partial_0|_e$ and $v_2:=\sqrt{2}\partial_0|_e+\partial_1|_e$. The flat metric gives $\eta(v_i,v_i)=-1$ and $\eta(v_i,N_e)<0$ for $i=1,2$, while $v_1\ne v_2$. Put $p_i:=e-v_i\in O$. Their flow lines have $\gamma_{p_i}(s)=e-(1-s)v_i$ for $0\le s<1$ and $W(\gamma_{p_i}(s))=v_i$; both base curves tend to $e$ as $s\uparrow1$, but the two limits of $W$ are distinct. A continuous extension of $W$ to $e$ would have to take both values $v_1$ and $v_2$, which is impossible. Thus this smooth congruence has no continuous, hence no smooth, extension through $e$; the individual affine geodesics still continue in $A$. This proves the local nonextension directly, independent of continuation beyond the region to which the hypotheses of [L5] apply.

(No singularity.) By [L1] the curvature and the Ricci tensor of the model vanish identically, every maximal geodesic of the model is a straight coordinate line with domain all of $\mathbb R$, and at $s=\rho(p)$ all flow lines pass through the single event $e$; the field $W$ is not defined at $e$ because $\rho(e)=0$. Hence the finite-time breakdown of the congruence in step 3.1 is exactly the focal crossing of the flow lines at $e$, while the spacetime and each individual geodesic continue; the example therefore shows that the local focusing theorem's conclusion is sharp and must be read as a statement about the congruence, not as a singularity. This proves (v) and completes the example.

citations.quote:
Let $A:=\mathbb R^4$ carry the flat structure $(\eta,N)$ of
[[def-gr-flat-minkowski-model-and-inertial-charts]], with global inertial
chart $x=(x^0,z)$ and translations $\tau_\lambda(p)=p+\lambda$ of clause (d),
and write $e_0:=(1,0,0,0)\in A$. Fix $L>0$, let
$\Lambda:=\{nLe_0:n\in\mathbb Z\}\subseteq A$ act on $A$ by the translations
$\tau_\lambda(p)=p+\lambda$ and fix $o\in A$
(the action of the discrete group $\mathbb Z$, equipped with its discrete
smooth structure, is a special case of the actions of
[[def-free-and-proper-lie-group-actions]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be the quotient
time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold produced by
[[lem-gr-quotient-by-isometric-free-proper-action]], with orbit map
$q:A\to M$. Then:

**(a)** $q$ is a local isometry: $g_{q(p)}(dq_pV,dq_pW)=\eta_p(V,W)$ for all
$p\in A$ and $V,W\in T_pA$; and $(M,g)$ is flat, in the sense that every
point has a chart in which the metric components are the constants
$\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and the curvature tensor of the
metric-selected connection vanishes identically.

**(b)** The curve $\gamma:\mathbb R\to M$, $\gamma(s):=q(o+se_0)$, is a
nonconstant smooth future timelike curve with $\gamma(s+L)=\gamma(s)$ for
all $s$; hence $(M,g,N)$ is neither chronological nor causal, and it
possesses a closed future timelike curve.

**(c)** Every two points $p,q\in M$ (equal or distinct) satisfy $p\ll q$:
the model is totally vicious. Consequently no subset of $M$ with two
distinct points is achronal or acausal.

**(d)** $M$ admits no Cauchy set and hence no Cauchy hypersurface in the
sense of [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]].

**(a) The underlying manifold.** Let $M:=\mathbb R^4$ be Euclidean four-space
as a set and real vector space ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), equipped
with its standard smooth structure, in which the identity map
$x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3):M\to\mathbb R^4$ is a global smooth chart
([[def-smooth-manifold]],
[[prop-open-subsets-of-euclidean-space-have-the-standard-smooth-structure]]).
The coordinate vector fields $\partial_a:=\partial/\partial x^a$,
$a=0,1,2,3$, are smooth vector fields on $M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]), and at every
$p\in M$ the tuple
$(\partial_0|_p,\partial_1|_p,\partial_2|_p,\partial_3|_p)$ is a basis of
$T_pM$ ([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]).

**(b) The metric.** The **flat metric** $\eta$ is the smooth covariant
$2$-tensor field on $M$ whose components in the chart $x$ are the constant
functions $\eta_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]), that is
$$\eta=-(dx^0)^2+(dx^1)^2+(dx^2)^2+(dx^3)^2 .$$
It is symmetric, and at every $p$ its matrix in the basis of (a) is
$\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$: diagonal, with one negative and three positive
entries and no zero entry. Hence $\eta_p$ is nondegenerate with inertia
$(3,1,0)$, that is, a Lorentz form on $T_pM$
([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]), and $(M,\eta)$ is a smooth Lorentzian
four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). The restriction of $\eta_p$ to
$\operatorname{span}(\partial_1|_p,\partial_2|_p,\partial_3|_p)$ is positive
definite.

**(c) Time orientation.** The field $N:=\partial_0$ satisfies
$\eta(N,N)=-1<0$ pointwise, so $N$ is a time orientation of $(M,\eta)$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] clause (c)). The triple $(M,\eta,N)$ is
the **flat model**. At every $p$ the pointwise vocabulary of
[[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] and
[[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]] applies, and a nonzero causal
$v\in T_pM$ is future-directed exactly when $\eta_p(v,N_p)<0$
([[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]).

**(d) Events, displacements and straight paths.** The points of $M$ are the
**events** of the model. Since $M=\mathbb R^4$ is a vector space, for events
$p,q\in M$ the **displacement** from $p$ to $q$ is the vector $q-p\in M$, and
the **straight path** from $p$ to $q$ is the curve $s\mapsto p+s(q-p)$ on
$[0,1]$, whose chart representative has the constant velocity $q-p$. For
$v\in\mathbb R^4$ the **translation** is the map $\tau_v(p):=p+v$ of $M$.

**(e) Inertial charts and frames.** A chart of $M$ with domain $M$ is called a
**global chart**. A global chart $y=(y^0,y^1,y^2,y^3):M\to\mathbb R^4$ is
**inertial** when its components of $\eta$ are the constant functions
$\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ on $M$ and its first coordinate vector field
$\partial/\partial y^0$ is future-directed at every point. The chart $x$ of (a)
is inertial: its components of $\eta$ are $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ by
(b), and its first coordinate vector field is $N$, future-directed by (c). If
$y$ is inertial and $o\in M$, the tuple
$(o;\partial/\partial y^0|_o,\partial/\partial y^1|_o,
\partial/\partial y^2|_o,\partial/\partial y^3|_o)$ is an **inertial frame**
at $o$; its vectors satisfy
$\eta(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ and $e_0$ is
future-directed.

**(f) Cone sets.** Let a vector $v\in T_pM$ have coordinates
$(v^0,v^1,v^2,v^3)$ in an inertial chart, write $v_s:=(v^1,v^2,v^3)$ and
$|v_s|:=\sqrt{(v^1)^2+(v^2)^2+(v^3)^2}$
([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). Write
$$C^+:=\{v\in\mathbb R^4:v^0>|v_s|\}$$
and $\overline{C^+}:=\{v\in\mathbb R^4:v^0\ge|v_s|\}$ for the coordinate cone
sets. In every inertial chart and at every event $p$,
the future cone $C_p^+$ of (c) consists of exactly those $v$ with
$v^0>|v_s|$, its closure of exactly those with $v^0\ge|v_s|$, and the
future-directed causal vectors of $T_pM$ are exactly the nonzero vectors with
$v^0\ge|v_s|$; moreover the future cone is closed under sums. All of this is
proved in [[lem-gr-flat-inertial-cone-criterion-and-sums]], where the
independence of the inertial chart is also established.

**(g) Scope.** This is a mathematical definition; it asserts nothing about
nature. The physical reading of the flat model is recorded with the framework
postulates of this library and is not part of this definition, and the flat
examples and counterexamples of this page are conditional statements inside
the model.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with the
causal curves and the relations $\le$, $\ll$, $I^{\pm}$, $J^{\pm}$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. All curves below are curves in
that sense.

**(a) Chronology and causality.** $(M,g,N)$ is **chronological** when there is
no $p\in M$ with $p\ll p$, equivalently when there is no nonconstant future
timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)$. It is **causal**
when there is no nonconstant future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with
$\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)$; a nonconstant future causal curve with equal endpoints
is called a **closed causal curve**, and a closed future timelike curve is
called a **closed timelike curve**.

**(b) Strong causality.** $(M,g,N)$ is **strongly causal** when for every
$p\in M$ and every open set $U\subseteq M$ with $p\in U$ there is an open set
$V$ with $p\in V\subseteq U$ such that for every future causal curve
$\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ and all $a\le s<t\le b$ with $\gamma(s)\in V$ and
$\gamma(t)\in V$ one has $\gamma([s,t])\subseteq V$. Thus no causal curve can
leave $V$ and later re-enter it; a set $V$ with this property for all causal
curves is called **causally convex for causal curves that meet it twice**.

**(c) Global hyperbolicity.** $(M,g,N)$ is **globally hyperbolic** when it is
strongly causal and for all $p,q\in M$ the **causal diamond**
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ is compact in the subspace topology
([[def-compact-space]]).

**(d) Time functions.** A **time function** on $(M,g,N)$ is a function
$u:M\to\mathbb R$ which is continuous ([[def-continuity-real]]) and satisfies
$u(\gamma(a))<u(\gamma(b))$ for every future causal curve
$\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $a<b$ that is not constant on $[a,b]$.

**(e) Temporal functions.** A **temporal function** on $(M,g,N)$ is a smooth
function $u:M\to\mathbb R$ ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]])
whose gradient is past-directed timelike: writing $du$ for its differential
([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]) and $\nabla u$ for the vector field
with $g(\nabla u,X)=du(X)$ for every smooth vector field $X$, constructed from
the inverse metric of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]], one
has
$$g(\nabla u,\nabla u)<0\qquad\text{and}\qquad du(N)=g(\nabla u,N)>0 .$$
The first inequality says that the gradient is nowhere zero and timelike; the
second fixes it as past-directed for the chosen time orientation. No level set
of a temporal function is asserted here to be a hypersurface or to be
spacelike, and no relation between temporal functions and compactness is
asserted; those claims are proved separately where they are used.

**(f) Scope and conventions.** These are mathematical conditions on the
Lorentzian model. Different sources define global hyperbolicity by equivalent
but differently phrased conditions; this page fixes the formulation of (c)
and proves the implications it uses. In particular no equivalence between
global hyperbolicity and the existence of a Cauchy hypersurface is asserted
by this definition, and the physical reading of strong causality or global
hyperbolicity as predictability of a classical model is adopted only in the
framework postulates.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), with the pointwise causal
classification of [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] and the
equivalence of "future-directed" with "pairing negatively with $N$" supplied by
[[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]. All curves below
take values in $M$; the physical reading of the model is not part of this
definition.

**(a) The curve class.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty
interior ([[def-interval]]) and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a map. A **chart
representative** of $\gamma$ is the map $x\circ\gamma$ of a smooth chart
$(U,x)$ of $M$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). The map $\gamma$ is
**locally absolutely continuous** when for every compact subinterval
$[a,b]\subseteq I$ and every chart $(U,x)$ with
$\gamma([a,b])\subseteq U$, the component map $x\circ\gamma$ is absolutely
continuous on $[a,b]$ in the sense of [[def-absolutely-continuous-function]].
This class does not depend on the chart or on the smooth atlas; that is proved
in [[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (a).

**(b) Velocity and causal curves.** Let $\gamma$ be locally absolutely
continuous and let $t$ be an interior point of $I$ at which some — equivalently
every — chart representative is differentiable. The **velocity**
$\gamma'(t)\in T_{\gamma(t)}M$ is the derivation whose components in a chart
$(U,x)$ around $\gamma(t)$ are
$\gamma'(t)=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\frac{d}{dt}(x^a\circ\gamma)(t)\,\partial_a|_{\gamma(t)}$
([[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]],
[[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]); it is independent of the
chart by the chain rule, as recorded in
[[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (b). A **future causal curve** is a
locally absolutely continuous $\gamma$ such that the set of $t\in I$ for which
$\gamma'(t)$ exists, is nonzero and is future causal is of full measure in
$I$ (its complement meets every compact subinterval of $I$ in a set of
Lebesgue measure zero). A **future timelike curve** (also called future
chronological) is defined in the same way with "future causal" replaced by
"future timelike". Past-directed versions are defined with $g_p(v,N_p)>0$.
Since a future causal nonzero vector is nonzero by definition, the velocity is
required to be nonzero at almost every parameter value; in particular no
nondegenerate subinterval of $I$ can be mapped to a single point
([[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (c)).

**(c) Reachability.** For events $p,q\in M$ define:

- $p\le q$, read "$q$ is in the future of $p$", when $p=q$, or when there are
  $a<b$ and a future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and
  $\gamma(b)=q$;
- $p\ll q$, read "$p$ chronologically precedes $q$", when there are $a<b$ and
  a future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and
  $\gamma(b)=q$.

The **causal future** and **chronological future** of a subset $S\subseteq M$
are
$$J^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}J^+(p),\qquad I^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}I^+(p),$$
where $J^+(p):=\{q\in M:p\le q\}$ and $I^+(p):=\{q\in M:p\ll q\}$; past
versions are $J^-(S):=\{p:\exists q\in S,\ p\in J^+(q)\}$ and
$I^-(S):=\{p:\exists q\in S,\ p\ll q\}$. By the displayed definition
$p\in J^+(p)$ for every $p$. Whether $p\in I^+(p)$ is a property of the
model, not a convention: $p\ll p$ holds exactly when there are $a<b$ and a
future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)=p$, that
is, exactly when a closed future timelike curve through $p$ exists. No
irreflexivity of $\ll$ is asserted, and closed timelike curves are not
excluded by the definition.

**(d) Inextendibility.** A locally absolutely continuous causal curve
$\gamma:I\to M$ is **future-inextendible** when $\gamma$ does not converge to
any point of $M$ as its parameter tends to $\sup I$, that is, there is no
$x\in M$ with $\gamma(t)\to x$ as $t\to\sup I$; in particular a curve whose
parameter range is unbounded above is future-inextendible exactly when it does
not converge as $t\to+\infty$. **Past-inextendible** is defined dually with
$\inf I$, and $\gamma$ is **inextendible** when it is both. This is the
convention of Minguzzi's Definition 2.16; for causal curves parametrized by
arclength of a complete auxiliary Riemannian metric it agrees with "the domain
cannot be extended", and a causal curve that converges at an endpoint can be
extended by a short geodesic segment, as proved in
[[lem-gr-maximal-geodesics-and-extension]] clauses (a) and (b). A causal
curve **passes through** $p$ when $p\in\gamma(I)$.

**(e) Scope.** The definitions are mathematical. They record no postulate
about nature, no measurement and no dynamical law; the physical reading of
$(M,g,N)$ and of the causal structure as the model's signalling structure is
adopted in the framework postulates and is not asserted here.

derivations.claim: (The witness is a future timelike curve.) By [L1] $\gamma$ is a smooth mapping into $M$ with velocity $\gamma'(s)=dq_{o+se_0}(\partial_0)$; the local isometry identity gives $g(\gamma',\gamma')=\eta(\partial_0,\partial_0)=-1<0$ and $g(\gamma',N)=\eta(\partial_0,\partial_0)=-1<0$, so every tangent is future unit timelike and $\gamma$ is a future timelike curve in the class of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]].

(The witness is closed and nonconstant on one period.) By [L1]
$\gamma(s+L)=q(o+se_0+Le_0)=q(o+se_0)=\gamma(s)$ because $Le_0\in\Lambda$. It is nonconstant on $[0,L]$: if $\gamma(s)=\gamma(0)$ for some $0<s<L$, then $se_0\in\Lambda$, so $s=nL$ for some nonzero integer $n$, which is impossible for $0<s<L$. Hence $\gamma|_{[0,L]}$ is a nonconstant future timelike curve with equal endpoints.

(Conclusion.) By step 1.2 and [L2] the model $(M,g,N)$ is not chronological: it contains a closed future timelike curve. Since $M$ is flat and time-oriented by [L1], this refutes the displayed statement. It also shows that a model with a closed timelike curve is not causal, and by [[thm-gr-flat-cylinder-closed-timelike-and-no-cauchy-set]] clause (d) it admits no Cauchy set at all.

Let $(M,\eta,N)$ be the flat model of
[[def-gr-flat-minkowski-model-and-inertial-charts]], with its global inertial
chart $x=(x^0,z)$, its cone sets $C^+,\overline{C^+}$ of clause (f) and its
translation action of clause (d), and with the causal relations of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. Then:

**(a)** For every $p\in M$, $J^+(p)=p+\overline{C^+}$ and
$I^+(p)=p+C^+$, where the sum is the translation of clause (d), the cone sets
are those of clause (f), and the displacement is read in the vector space
$M=\mathbb R^4$; in the chart,
$$q\in J^+(p)\Longleftrightarrow x^0(q)-x^0(p)\ge|z(q)-z(p)|_{\mathrm e}.$$

**(b)** For every $c\in\mathbb R$ the level set
$\Sigma_c:=x^{-1}(\{c\})$ is a spacelike embedded hypersurface of $M$, and
every inextendible causal curve of $M$ meets $\Sigma_c$ in exactly one
parameter value; equivalently, $\Sigma_c$ is a Cauchy hypersurface in the
sense of [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c).

**(c)** For all $p,q\in M$ the causal diamond $J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ is
compact.

**(d)** The model is strongly causal in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (b); hence it is
globally hyperbolic in the sense of clause (c) of that definition.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,\eta,N)$ be the
flat model of [[def-gr-flat-minkowski-model-and-inertial-charts]], with its
global inertial chart $x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, written $x=(x^0,z)$ with
$z\in\mathbb R^3$ (clauses (a), (b) and (e) of that definition), and let
$\gamma:I\to M$ be a future causal curve in the class of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. Then:

**(a)** $x^0\circ\gamma:I\to\mathbb R$ is strictly increasing.

**(b)** For all $a<b$ in $I$,
$$\bigl|z(\gamma(b))-z(\gamma(a))\bigr|\le x^0(\gamma(b))-x^0(\gamma(a)),$$
and consequently $\gamma$ is injective and its image is a $1$-Lipschitz graph
over the interval $(x^0\circ\gamma)(I)$.

**(c)** If $\gamma$ is future-inextendible then
$\sup\,(x^0\circ\gamma)(I)=+\infty$; if $\gamma$ is past-inextendible then
$\inf\,(x^0\circ\gamma)(I)=-\infty$. Hence if $\gamma$ is inextendible then
$x^0\circ\gamma$ is a strictly increasing surjection onto $\mathbb R$, and
for every $c\in\mathbb R$ the parameter set
$\{t\in I:x^0(\gamma(t))=c\}$ is a singleton.

**(d)** The coordinate function $u:=x^0$ is a temporal function of the flat
model in the sense of [[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]]
clause (e): its gradient is the vector field $\nabla u=-\partial_0$ on all of
$M$, with $\eta(\nabla u,\nabla u)=-1<0$ and $du(\partial_0)=1>0$
everywhere.

Let $M^m$ be a smooth manifold, let $k\in\mathbb N$ satisfy $0\le k\le m$,
and let $S\subseteq M$. One says that $S$ is an **embedded $k$-dimensional
submanifold** of $M$ when for every $p\in S$ there
is a smooth chart $\varphi:U\to\varphi(U)\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ with $p\in U$
such that

$$\varphi(S\cap U)=\varphi(U)\cap(\mathbb R^k\times\{0\}).$$

Such a chart is a **slice chart** for $S$ at $p$. The topology on $S$ is the
subspace topology inherited from $M$ ([[def-subspace-topology-top]]).

The next lemma proves that the restricted slice charts define a smooth
$k$-manifold structure on $S$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with the
causal curves of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]], and let
$S\subseteq M$.

**(a) Spacelike hypersurfaces.** A subset $\Sigma\subseteq M$ is a **spacelike
embedded hypersurface** when it is an embedded three-dimensional submanifold
of $M$ ([[def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart]]) such that the
restriction of $g_p$ to $T_p\Sigma\times T_p\Sigma$ is positive definite for
every $p\in\Sigma$; equivalently, every nonzero vector tangent to $\Sigma$ is
spacelike ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). A spacelike
embedded hypersurface is automatically a nondegenerate hypersurface, so its
$g$-orthogonal complement in $T_pM$ is one-dimensional and nondegenerate, and
it carries a unique future-directed unit timelike normal; that normal is
constructed where it is used, not here.

**(b) Achronality and acausality.** $S$ is **achronal** when no two distinct
points $p,q\in S$ satisfy $p\ll q$ or $q\ll p$; $S$ is **acausal** when no two
distinct points $p,q\in S$ satisfy $p\le q$ or $q\le p$. Every acausal set is
achronal, since $p\ll q$ implies $p\le q$.

**(c) Cauchy sets.** $S$ is a **Cauchy set** when for every inextendible
causal curve $\gamma:I\to M$ the parameter set
$$\gamma^{-1}[S]:=\{t\in I:\gamma(t)\in S\}$$
has exactly one element. Because a strictly increasing continuous surjection
of intervals induces a bijection of parameter sets, this condition is
invariant under reparametrization
([[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (e)); it is stated in terms of
parameters rather than of the point set $\gamma(I)\cap S$, so that a closed
causal curve counts two visits to the same point as two parameter values. A
**Cauchy hypersurface** is a Cauchy set that is also a spacelike embedded
hypersurface in the sense of clause (a).

**(d) Domains of dependence.** For any $S\subseteq M$ define
$$D^+(S):=\{p\in M:\text{every past-inextendible causal curve through }p \text{ meets }S\},$$
and dually $D^-(S):=\{p\in M:\text{every future-inextendible causal curve
through }p\text{ meets }S\}$, where "meets $S$" means that some parameter
value is mapped into $S$, and $D(S):=D^+(S)\cup D^-(S)$ is the **domain of
dependence** of $S$.

**(e) Cauchy horizon.** For a closed set $S\subseteq M$ the **future Cauchy
horizon** is
$$H^+(S):=D^+(S)\setminus I^-(D^+(S)),$$
the set of points of $D^+(S)$ that are not chronologically preceded by any
point of $D^+(S)$; dually $H^-(S):=D^-(S)\setminus I^+(D^-(S))$, and the
**Cauchy horizon** is $H(S):=H^+(S)\cup H^-(S)$.

**(f) Scope.** These are mathematical definitions. Neither existence of
Cauchy sets nor any relation between the objects defined here is asserted.

**(f) Scope.** These are mathematical definitions. Neither existence of

derivations.claim: (The set is spacelike.) By [L3] the set $\Sigma$ is an embedded three-dimensional submanifold of $A$ with tangent space spanned by $\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_3$, on which $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(1,1,1)$ is positive definite; hence $\Sigma$ is a spacelike embedded hypersurface.

(An inextendible causal curve missing it.) Define $u:\mathbb R\to A$, $u(s):=x^{-1}(s,z_0)$. This is a smooth curve with constant tangent $\partial_0=N$, which satisfies $\eta(\partial_0,\partial_0)=-1<0$ and is future-directed by clause (c) of [[def-gr-flat-minkowski-model-and-inertial-charts]], so $u$ is a future timelike (hence causal) curve; its $t$-coordinate is the identity of $\mathbb R$, so it has no point limit at either infinite parameter end: such a limit would force its continuous real time coordinate to have a finite limit. Thus $u$ is inextendible by [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (d). But $t(u(s))=s$ and $z(u(s))=z_0$ with $|z_0|_{\mathrm e}=2>1$, so $u(s)\notin\Sigma$ for every $s$; the parameter set $\{s:u(s)\in\Sigma\}$ is empty and in particular not a singleton.

(Conclusion.) By step 1.2 there is an inextendible causal curve that meets $\Sigma$ in no parameter value; by [L4] the set $\Sigma$ is not a Cauchy set, and by step 1.1 it is a spacelike embedded hypersurface, so it is not a Cauchy hypersurface. Since the ambient model is globally hyperbolic by [L1], this refutes the displayed statement: in a globally hyperbolic model a spacelike hypersurface need not be Cauchy.

step 1.1 uses the straight path on the closed parameter interval [0,1] joining the two null-related events.
steps 1.1 and 3.1 fix the two events explicitly; no selection over a family is made.
